title: Getting on the Map: The Impact of Online Listings on Business Performance
eligible_reason: Full-sample design: establishments are added to Yelp in different quarters (binary treat_q = listed on Yelp in this quarter, ~42 adoption quarters in the sample, with never-listed establishments as controls), estimated by Gardner's did2s two-stage estimator with establishment and quarter (or county x quarter) fixed effects and no covariates; a reghdfe TWFE counterpart (post_yelp) is in table2c.do. The bulk-add natural experiment is a single adoption date and is not eligible.
design_notes: Panel of bars/restaurants at the establishment (locid) x quarter level, 44 quarters (Stata quarter codes 188-231, i.e. 2007q1-2017q4), outcome lntot_rec = log quarterly tax receipts. Treatment treat_q = 1 if the business is on Yelp in that quarter (quarter_added = quarter the listing was created; missing for never-listed). Two samples: fullsample_for_r_sample (all listings, staggered adoption, 42 distinct quarter_added in the scrambled 20% sample, 22% of rows never listed) and bulkadd_for_r_sample (establishments added in one bulk data acquisition plus never-listed establishments; quarter_added takes a single value, so this is a one-cohort design and ineligible). Estimator: did2s(yname = lntot_rec, first_stage = ~0 | locid + quarter or locid + county_quarter, second_stage = ~i(treat_q, ref = 0), treatment = treat_q, cluster_var = locid). Table 2b and Figure 2b repeat the analysis on the CEM-matched subsample (matched1 == 1), which is matching-based and excluded. Table 3 splits the full sample by chain status, tourist area, size and rating (split-sample regressions, no interactions). table2c.do (not listed in the README) runs reghdfe lntot_rec post_yelp with post_yelp = (quarter > quarter_added), absorb(locid quarter) and absorb(locid county_quarter), cluster locid, for both samples; its location in the paper is unknown (possibly an OLS panel of Table 2 or an appendix). IMPORTANT: the README states the package data are a 20% random sample with key variables shuffled (quarter, quarter_added, county, lntot_rec, county_quarter, relquarter) and that results do not replicate with these files; the scrambling also produces duplicate locid-quarter rows. The original data are proprietary (Yelp plus confidential tax records).
estimators_reported: TWFE static (reghdfe, table2c.do; location in paper unclear)

data_files_note: Three .dta files are present (master_panel_sample 196,722 x 21; fullsample_for_r_sample 54,454 x 13; bulkadd_for_r_sample 42,273 x 13) but they are a 20% sample with shuffled key variables; README: 'our results do not replicate using this scrambled data'.

screener_notes: Eligible design with clean no-covariate did2s and TWFE specifications, but replication requires the authors' unscrambled Yelp + tax-record panel; contact authors. If data are obtained: idname = locid, tname = quarter, gname = quarter_added (0 for never-listed), cluster = locid; TWFE counterparts feols(lntot_rec ~ treat_q | locid + quarter) and | locid + county_quarter. Confirm with the article whether table2c.do's OLS results appear in the main text (if not, n_eligible_specs = 11).
